## Simple explanation

Python is a programming language with readable syntax and a large ecosystem
of libraries. AI engineers use it to explore data, build models, automate
workflows, and connect AI services to applications.

## Technical explanation

Python is a high-level, dynamically typed language with multiple
programming paradigms. Its implementations and extension interfaces allow
performance-critical libraries to use compiled code while exposing
convenient Python APIs.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Many data, machine-learning, and model-serving tools provide Python
interfaces. This makes it practical to move from experimentation to
production integration, while teams still need to manage dependencies,
performance, testing, and deployment environments.

## How it works

Python source is typically compiled to bytecode and executed by an
interpreter. Packages extend the standard library with domain-specific
functionality. In numerical and deep-learning libraries, substantial
computation may run in optimized native kernels rather than Python loops.

## Practical example

An engineer can load a dataset, split it into training and validation sets,
fit a classifier using a Python machine-learning library, and expose
predictions through an API. A lockfile or pinned environment helps reproduce
the setup.

## Common misconceptions

- Python is not always slow: numerical work may be delegated to optimized
  native libraries, though Python-level overhead can still matter.
- A script that runs on one machine is not automatically reproducible or
  deployable; dependencies and environment details matter.
